note: Re-read the full RFC 9069 section 6.1.1 emulated-peer obligation, the current TestLocRIBSinglePeerUpPerInstance, its complete stored-path fixtures, and both Peer Up producers. Two valid best-change batches with distinct prefixes and next hops must produce exactly one Loc-RIB Peer Up plus two non-End-of-RIB Route Monitoring messages; the test reads all three and fails on no peer or a duplicate per-source peer. Its one-shot assertion is stricter than the required at-least-one lower bound for Ze's single supported Loc-RIB instance. The single-polarity annotation correctly names the shared per-collector senderSession.locRIBUpSent guard in ensureLocRIBPeerUp/primeLocRIBPeerUp; both feed producers construct the same emulated instance, rather than exposing a separate input-selected peer-creation mode. Runtime admission now checks validateLocRIBRuntimeConfig before any startup mutation and before any reload candidate is published: a process without the RIB event bus refuses a requested Loc-RIB configuration with its cause and exact internal-plugin remedy. It therefore does not accept an instance whose required peer/dump cannot exist. Supported available-bus monitoring retains the subscription, initial replay and actual collector delivery checked by the existing initial-dump test. The main-thread external functional proof now observes the exact unavailable-bus refusal and internal-plugin remedy, successful daemon SSH, and absence of the refused BMP process from the real subsystem list. The main-thread internal functional proof observes a complete Peer Type 3 UPDATE over the collector transport; its generic collector does not itself assert a prefix or Peer Up ordering. The exact one-peer/two-route count and replayed-prefix delivery assertions remain in the independently read unit collector tests, which also passed in the main-thread full BMP run. These together discharge the runtime-mode concern without changing the daemon's existing nonfatal plugin-refusal policy.
